**Notes**

- **Why the roster is one row.** The US roster is every S&P 500 constituent plus every US-listed
- name above the $50B floor, intersected with three independent calendars (EarningsWhispers 209 names, Nasdaq 218 rows, Yahoo Finance).
- The live Wikipedia constituent list parses to **503** symbols with all three symbol templates (NyseSymbol, NasdaqSymbol, BZX link) and the control tickers BRK.B, GOOGL, GOOG, FOX and CBOE all present.
- Only **VYLR** survives as an S&P 500 constituent reporting today, and **no** US-listed name above $50B prints - the only names over that line on the calendar are OTC ADR lines of non-US issuers (IFNNY, EONGY, RWEOY, LBLCF), which belong in the non-US universe, not in this table.

- **VYLR is in the roster on membership, not size.** Vylor joined the S&P 500 on 2026-10-01
- (Consumer Staples / Agricultural Products, CIK 212862). Its $48.4B cap sits below the $50B floor;
- the Nasdaq calendar carries $46.8B for the same name, a 3.4% spread that is inside tolerance and does not change the floor test.
- Flag is `-`: a row inside the floor by less than $0.5B carries `boundary_case`, and VYLR is not inside the floor at all.

- **Reaction columns are degraded on VYLR, and that is a real gap, not a fetch failure.**
- Nasdaq's earnings-surprise endpoint returns **zero** past report dates for VYLR - it is a newly listed entity with no earnings history - so `Avg abs move %` and `Prior result` are `n/a` and no composite score can be computed.
- `reaction_degraded: 1` records exactly that one row.
- The implied move **is** measured: a Cboe ATM straddle at strike 75.00 against the 2026-11-20 expiry (the first expiry that straddles the event) is 6.48% of the $72.53 close.
- With a single row and no score, no reaction ranking could be established today - the table is not sorted by score because there is only one row.

- **Two aggregator dates were wrong and both names were dropped.** EarningsWhispers carried
- **IFNNY (Infineon)** as BMO on Nov 11;
- Infineon's own press release and TDnet timestamp show it published its FY2026 Q4 on **10 November 07:30 CET**, which is the 10 November ET day.
- Nasdaq carried **TECH (Bio-Techne)**; its 8-K (Nov 4) and 10-Q (Nov 6) show Q1 FY2027 was already reported on Nov 5. Neither appears in this artifact.

- **Loblaw is not a November 11 name either.** Its own press release (Oct 22) says Q3 2026
results come on **November 19, 2026** at approx. 06:30 ET. EarningsWhispers' Nov 11 BMO entry for LBLCF is wrong.

- **Poste Italiane is deliberately excluded.** Its own 2026 corporate events calendar splits the
- Q3 event across two days:
- the board approves the interim report on operations at 30 September 2026 on **Nov 11**, and the Q3 & 9M-26 Group Results presentation is **Nov 12, 11:00 CET** (= Nov 12, 05:00 ET).
- The results announcement therefore falls on the **12 November ET day**, and the Nov 11 entry carries no published local time to convert, so it is not published here.

- **Checked and not published:** Nan Ya Plastics (TWSE 1303, $69.5B) carries an aggregator
earnings date on Nov 11 but no issuer-confirmed ET announcement time and no US line.

- **The four names printed before the fire appear twice on purpose.** They are listed in the
- non-US table for their reference data (primary listing, venue, US line, status) and again in the "Already reported" table for the published figures.
- No issuer appears twice inside the three contract tables.

- **Count definitions:** `pending_count: 2` = published names still ahead (VYLR, POW.TO);
`already_reported_count: 4` = names that printed before the 06:00 ET fire; `non_us_count: 5` = rows in the non-US table.

- **Band caveats.** The band is a **lower bound** on what the $50B floor excluded - names below
- $40B are excluded by the band, not by the floor. Twelve names qualify once depositary-receipt lines (TradingView type `dr`) and preferreds, notes, bonds, warrants, rights and units are filtered out;
- the ten largest are published and SLF ($40.9B) and HEI ($40.8B) sit just below the cut.
- That same filter is why the ADR lines in the band (INFY, MT, NOK, VALE, SE, HMC, ABEV, ONC, WDS) are absent - they are depositary receipts, and their issuers are covered by the non-US universe when they report.

- **Ticker convention.** Primary listing first with its exchange suffix; the US line follows in
parentheses or in `us_peer`. No OTC or ADR line is ever the headline. Foreign amounts are published in the issuer's own currency and labelled.

- **Cadence and reliability of the calendars.** EarningsWhispers publishes a per-day calendar
- and **rolls a company forward** once it has reported (its IFNNY page now points at Nov 18) - its dates are a screening list, not a source of truth.
- Nasdaq's calendar is a same-day snapshot with a market cap, an EPS forecast and a BMO/AMC flag, but **no revenue** and a `time-not-supplied` value on some rows.
- Yahoo's calendar carries EPS but no revenue.
- Issuer IR pages are the only authority for a date and a local announcement time, and every row published here was confirmed on one.

- **Degraded source.** Yahoo's quote API (`v7/finance/quote`, `quoteSummary`) returned
- **HTTP 429 rate-limited** for the whole run from this egress.
- A 429 is a rate limit, not an absence: market caps were taken from the TradingView scanner instead and EPS/revenue from the Yahoo and Nasdaq calendar and analysis pages.
- No published field was left unmeasured.

- **Limitations.** The reaction layer needs prior earnings history, so on a day with one
S&P 500 constituent the screen has almost no surface. Consensus "vs consensus" cells are `n/a` where no consensus figure was sourced in this run - they are not estimated.

**Rules applied**

- S&P 500 membership verified against the live constituent list (503 symbols, all three symbol
templates parsed, control tickers checked) - never from memory.

- Every published report date confirmed on an issuer-owned page; aggregator-only dates were not
published, and every date-confirmed exclusion is recorded in the Notes.

- Reaction columns measured from Yahoo daily bars and the Cboe delayed chain. A column that could
not be measured is published as `n/a` and counted in `reaction_degraded` - never estimated from market cap, a peer name, or a guess.

- The roster is ranked by reaction potential, not by market cap; with one row and no derivable
score, no ordering was available.

- Primary listing first with its exchange suffix; no OTC or ADR ticker is ever the headline, and
local-currency amounts carry their currency.

- The three contract tables do not overlap, and no issuer is published twice inside them.
- The $50B floor is published with the band it excludes, and a row inside the floor by less than
$0.5B carries `boundary_case` (none today).

- Local announcement times converted with `zoneinfo` and compared against the fire's scheduled
instant (2026-11-11 06:00 ET), never against the wall clock.
